parts.transcript: S1: William interviews Grace for volunteer work. Email graceb@travel.co.nz (1). Used to be in teaching, has a diploma in teaching (2; was also a bank teller). Can't start before 8.15 or work past 3; agreed hours 9.15am to 2pm Mon-Fri, so from 9.15 (3). Experience: volunteer city guide at the Rugby World Cup in Auckland (4); volunteer netball team coach at university (5). Hobbies: works in her garden (6), flower arranging, plays the guitar (7, would like to try flute). Work offered: helping on a farm (8) for a month, or community centre with elderly people. Why volunteer: wants to make more friends (9) + help others. Heard about agency: saw an advertisement at the supermarket (10).

parts.transcript: S2: owner Peter Blakewell briefs new employees at the strawberry farm. Bring your own water (11=C; lunch/sandwiches provided, gloves at the packing shed). parts.transcript: S3: engineering student Kathy and her tutor discuss her dissertation on water pumps. Tutor read her first/introductory chapter (21=B). Liked the clear overall structure/organisation (22=A; sentences too long/complex). She needs to take additional measurements = record more data (23=B; more library work NOT essential; topic range already well judged). Tutor shares how he got his first research post by approaching a visiting professor - to encourage Kathy to do similar (chat with James Higgins) (24=C). She'll handle the bibliography herself but wants guidance on the appendices (25=C). Next she'll investigate the latest CAD software (26=A). Activities->benefits: Mechanical Engineers' Society meetings = networking/make useful contacts (27=F); visiting different workplaces = keep up-to-date with the cutting edge (28=C); work experience abroad = broadens practical experience (29=A); international conference = present her dissertation = publicise own work (30=B).

parts.transcript: S4: lecture on American salt marshes + the horseshoe crab. Salinity ranges from ocean (31) strength to almost fresh. The depth (32) and warmth of the water change through the day. Worms and shrimps feed on the plants (33) growing in the marsh. 200 years ago marshland was used for rice (34) cultivation. Artificial walls/dikes restrict water movement so the natural habitat of aquatic life is reduced = wildlife has less space (35=B). People complain about dikes because access for walkers is reduced (36=A; not beauty, insects happy). In the mid-20th century over half the marshes were destroyed, filled to create land for housing = residential areas (37=B). State laws now protect marshes as a barrier limiting land lost to the sea = prevent erosion of soil (38=A). Horseshoe crab: main food = shellfish (39, also worms); female lays eggs in spring (40, before the sand heats up).
